statusText: Green. A weekend escalation in the Strait of Hormuz and a hawkish Fed repricing sit against an orderly, two-way reopen tape, so Stress rises into the moderate band while Tail stays low and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains well below the block threshold across the whole projected window, with a conditional peak of 17 at the 31 August U.S. cash open. One narrow observation window is flagged across 13:30-14:30 UTC on 31 August, where month-end rebalancing imbalance meets the first U.S. cash test of Friday's front-end repricing and the weekend Hormuz strike. A secondary conditional flag sits on the 00:00-01:00 UTC Asia-Pacific open, the first deep-liquidity test of the geopolitical headline. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: a Hormuz escalation and rising hike odds meet a reopen tape that still retraces
body:
The Nasdaq-100 September contract has now traded a full ninety minutes since the CME weekly reopen, and the shape of that trade is the most important evidence in this assessment. The contract reopened at 29,540.00, was rejected within five points at a 29,545.50 high, and has ground steadily lower to a session low of 29,405.75, last changing hands near 29,412 for a loss of 79.75 points, or 0.27%, against Friday's 29,491.75 settlement. The session range is 139.75 points, about 0.47% of the index. The tilt is unmistakably lower and the highs are successively lower, but the path is not the pathological one: the dip into 29,428.00 at 22:40 UTC drew a 25-point bounce to 29,453.50, the slide into 29,428.75 at 23:00 UTC drew a bounce to 29,449.25, and the break to the low at 23:10 UTC was itself bought back ten points. Retracements are occurring at every step, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines a mean-reversion failure. S&P 500 futures are tracking the same contained pattern at 7,705.00, and Dow futures are down 0.14%.

What has changed since the previous assessment is the news backdrop rather than the tape. U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, the first military action there in roughly a month, after IRGC units were observed preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the strait. The IRGC has confirmed casualties and warned that the strike will be met with a retaliatory response. Crude has responded: WTI is near $84.83 having traded as high as $85.68, and the geopolitical premium is intact. That is a genuine discontinuity with an unresolved second leg, and it is the single largest reason Stress rises to 41 in the moderate band.

The monetary backdrop compounds it. Chairman Warsh used his Jackson Hole remarks on Friday to say that the summer's better PCE and CPI readings do not tell him underlying trends have meaningfully improved, with the twelve-month PCE change at 3.7%. Fed funds futures now price roughly a 57% chance of a 25 basis point hike in September, up from about 35% the day before. The two-year yield jumped more than twelve basis points to around 4.36% on Friday and the ten-year rose four basis points to 4.72%, against H.15 constant-maturity readings of 4.20% and 4.67% on 27 August. Treasury futures are marginally lower again on the reopen, so the front-end repricing has not reversed overnight.

Against those amplifiers stand two arguments for keeping Tail low. First, the observed path retraces, and the overlay's own precedent is that hypothetical post-event alignment is not evidence until it is priced. Second, Friday's internals were rotational rather than one-way: semiconductors fell hard across the board, with Nvidia down 4.57%, Arm down 6.33% and semiconductor equipment off 3.96%, while Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet all closed between 1.2% and 4.0% higher. Conflicting breadth of that kind cuts directional conviction and raises uncertainty; it does not mechanically manufacture a trend. The VIX closed Friday at 14.43, a year-to-date low, with volatility futures only modestly firmer on the reopen.

Tail is therefore scored at 14, Stress at 41 and Confidence at 87, with dominant mode mixed: a soft directional drift coexisting with two-way trade and rotational internals. The conditional path lifts to 16 across the Asia-Pacific open, the first deep-liquidity test of the Hormuz headline, eases through the Asian session, holds near the trough across a European morning thinned by the London Summer Bank Holiday, and peaks at 17 across the 13:30 UTC cash open, where month-end rebalancing imbalance on the final August session meets the first U.S. cash verdict on both stories. A second lift to 15 covers the 20:00 UTC month-end closing auction. Tail remains below the block threshold at every hour of the projected window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, running from the Saturday evening weekend halt through the hour containing the CME weekly reopen. Twenty-three of those hours sat inside the closed market with Tail fixed at the halt floor of 5, dominant mode normal and status green throughout, while Stress drifted gradually from 25 to 32 as the reopen approached and the weekend news flow accumulated. Confidence decayed to 58 by 04:00 UTC as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered steadily to 87 as primary sources were re-verified on each hourly refresh. Only the final slot, the 22:00 UTC hour containing the reopen, carried live price structure, and it lifted Tail to 9 on the first observable two-way path since Friday.
outlookSummary: The current hour extends the reopen path into a session low of 29,405.75 while retracements continue to trade, so Tail is scored at 14 with Stress 41 and Confidence 87 against a weekend Hormuz escalation and a hawkish Fed repricing. The conditional path lifts to 16 across the 00:00-01:00 UTC Asia-Pacific open, the first deep-liquidity test of the geopolitical headline, then eases through the Asian session to a trough of 12 between 04:00 and 07:00 UTC. It holds near that trough through a European morning thinned by the London Summer Bank Holiday, lifts a notch across the mid-morning rate-desk repricing, and builds through the U.S. pre-market to a projected peak of 17 in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC cash open, where month-end rebalancing imbalance on the final August session meets the first U.S. cash test of both Friday's front-end move and the Hormuz strike. The Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC follows as a medium-impact checkpoint. Tail then decays through the afternoon before a second lift to 15 across the 20:00 UTC month-end closing auction, easing to 11 by the final projected hour. No hour in the projected window reaches the block threshold.

forecast.analysis: Observed this hour: the reopen high of 29,545.50 has given way to a session low of 29,405.75 and a last near 29,412, a 140-point range faded in both directions. The drift is directional but each 15-25 point bounce has traded, so no-retracement structure is absent and Tail stays in the low band.

forecast.analysis: Sydney and Tokyo bring the first broad-liquidity vote on the Hormuz strike. Conditional risk peaks for the overnight stretch here: an Iranian response headline landing in this window could price in one direction before depth returns. Absent that, the two-way reopen pattern is the base case.

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session. Conditional risk continues to normalise if no second geopolitical leg has materialised by this hour. Month-end positioning in Asia is typically mechanical rather than directional, which argues for range behaviour rather than persistent extension.

Assumption: no fresh escalation beyond the verified Larak Island strike
Crude stability would be the confirming cross-asset signal

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Conditional Tail holds at the trough. The London Summer Bank Holiday on 31 August removes UK cash participation for the whole session, so continental venues alone set the European tone and volumes are expected to run below a normal Monday.
drivers: UK Summer Bank Holiday closes London cash for the 31 August session
Continental-only European liquidity thins the morning order book

forecast.analysis: Frankfurt and Paris open into a holiday-thinned Europe. Conditional structure is expected to be range-bound; a genuine trend leg would need a fresh catalyst that is not on the calendar for this hour. Tail is held at the trough on that reasoning.
drivers: Continental European cash open without London as the depth anchor

forecast.analysis: European morning. Conditional Tail lifts a notch as European rate desks reprice Friday's hawkish U.S. front-end move for the first time this week. That repricing has, on Friday's evidence, expressed itself in yields and rotation rather than in index-level one-way structure.
